source_text: Multifarie multisque modis Deus locutus est patribus in prophetis. Aliquando ineffabilia sacramenta docet; aliquando de Salvatore instruit; interdum mores corrigit. Totus psalmus trigesimus sextus moralis est — cura et medicina humanae animae. Principium: Noli aemulari inter malignantes, neque aemulatus fueris facientes iniquitatem; quoniam sicut fenum cito arescent, et sicut olera herbarum cito decident.
thought_title: God's many ways of speaking and the moral medicine of Psalm 36
orientation: Origen opens the homily by describing how God spoke to the fathers through the prophets and introduces Psalm 36 as moral medicine for the human soul.
pass_a_gloss: In many parts and in many ways God spoke to the fathers in the prophets. Sometimes he teaches ineffable mysteries; sometimes he instructs about the Savior; sometimes he corrects morals. The whole thirty-sixth psalm is moral — care and medicine of the human soul. The beginning: Do not envy among the wicked, nor shall you have envied those who do iniquity; because like hay they will quickly wither, and like herbs of the field they will quickly fall.

choices.english: In many parts and in many ways
choices.why: Keeps the two adverbial phrases distinct and literal, matching the source's double emphasis on the varied manner of God's speech.
rejected: At many times and in many manners

choices.why: Renders the Latin term for hidden divine realities without importing later sacramental theology.

choices.english: care and medicine of the human soul
choices.why: Preserves the medical metaphor and the genitive relation exactly.
rejected: healing and remedy for the human soul
care and cure of the soul

choices.english: Do not envy among the wicked
choices.why: Uses the glossary rendering 'envy' for aemulari and keeps the prepositional phrase 'among the wicked' literal.
rejected: Do not be jealous of evildoers
Do not fret because of the wicked

choices.english: like hay they will quickly wither
choices.why: Keeps the simile and the future tense of the psalm quotation.
rejected: like grass they will soon dry up
as hay they will quickly fade

choices.english: like herbs of the field they will quickly fall
choices.why: Renders olera herbarum literally as 'herbs of the field' and keeps the verb 'fall' for decident.
rejected: like green plants they will soon die
like the green herb they will quickly wither

pass_b_english: God spoke to the fathers in the prophets in many parts and in many ways (Hebrews 1:1). Sometimes he teaches ineffable mysteries; sometimes he instructs about the Savior; sometimes he corrects behavior. The whole of Psalm 36 is moral—care and medicine of the human soul. Its beginning: Do not envy among the wicked, nor envy those who do iniquity; for like hay they will quickly wither, and like herbs of the field they will quickly fall (Psalm 37:1-2, LXX 36:1-2).

last_rejected.why: Citation format contradicts brief: should be Psalm 37 (LXX 36):1-2, not Psalm 37:1-2, LXX 36:1-2.
last_rejected.ruling: Source lacks any citation format; English correctly identifies Psalm 37:1-2 and LXX 36:1-2. Format preference is not a major error.
